newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army advances into Tamil rebel territory.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army advances into Tamil rebel territory.

text.p: Sri Lanka's army has launched its biggest offensive this year against rebel-held territory in the north and so far met no resistance, military officials and news reports said on Wednesday.
The move was launched from north-central Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) from Colombo, on Sri Lanka's Independence Day on Tuesday, said military officials in the north of the country and in the capital.

The Defence Ministry declined to comment and the military officials said they had no information on the exact number of troops. The Midweek Mirror newspaper said thousands of government soldiers were involved in the attack and the operation was the biggest this year.
The clandestine radio of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), monitored by Reuters, said 20,000 government troops were taking part in the offensive.
The army had encountered no resistance so far and LTTE guerrillas appear to be avoiding battle, said the military officials, who declined to be named.
Some military officials said the army was trying to link two government-held outposts -- the frontline town of Vavuniya and the town of Kilinochchi, 70 km (48 miles) to Vavuniya's north.
Other military officials said the army's aim was to open a supply route to isolated Mannar on the northwest coast after intelligence reports of a rebel build-up in the area.

Defence analysts said the army's real objective could be Kilinochchi, as part of its long-planned effort to open a supply route to the northern Jaffna peninsula and ultimately link Colombo with the entire northern part of the island.
The LTTE radio station said air and artillery strikes in the area had preceded the offensive, and spotter planes were seen circling the area. There were no reports of casualties.

Kilinochchi, a town that fell to the army last July, has been the focus of recent fighting between the two sides. Kilinochchi's only current supply route is a road linking it to Jaffna on the northern tip of the Indian Ocean island.
The government can supply Jaffna, the LTTE's main stronghold in the country until last year, only by air or sea.
Early last month, the LTTE launched an offensive against government forces in the north in a failed effort to block off the Jaffna-Kilinochchi road.

In three days of fighting starting on January 9, the government said it lost 160 soldiers while the LTTE said 140 of its fighters, including 78 women, had been killed. Both sides said their opponents had suffered higher death tolls.
The LTTE has waged war for a separate Tamil homeland in the country's north and east since 1983. LTTE spokesmen in Paris and London were not immediately available for comment.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the conflict but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
